test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Heat Engine) Official Paper (Held On 06 May, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: A man rides a bicycle from Point A to Point B in 10 minutes and comes back to Point B along the same path in 10 minutes. If the distance between Points A and B is 1 km, calculate his average velocity?
solution:
**Given:**

Distance between Points A and B = 1 km

Time taken from A to B = 10 minutes

Time taken from B to A = 10 minutes

**Formula Used:**

Average velocity = Total displacement / Total time

**Calculation:**

⇒ Total displacement = Final position - Initial position = 0 km (as the man comes back to the starting point)

⇒ Total time = 10 minutes + 10 minutes = 20 minutes = 20 × 60 seconds = 1200 seconds

⇒ Average velocity = Total displacement / Total time

⇒ Average velocity = 0 km / 1200 s = 0 m/s

**∴ The correct answer is 0 m/s.**
